prompt: What does leave-one-out validation estimate for a model trained on N examples?
accepted: average error when each point is held out once
solution: Train on N-1 examples, evaluate the held-out point, and average over all N choices of the held-out point.
hint: One example is omitted at a time.
explanation: LOO uses much of the data for each fit but can be computationally expensive and correlated across folds.
misconception: Evaluating one model on all points without retraining.

prompt: Why should the final test score not be used to select the best regularization parameter?
accepted: it leaks test information and makes the estimate optimistic
solution: Using the test score to choose $\lambda$ makes the test set part of training/model selection, so the reported score is no longer an unbiased final estimate.
hint: Ask what information influenced the chosen model.
explanation: A clean evaluation requires the test set to remain unseen until all choices are fixed.
misconception: Thinking only parameter gradients count as training information.
visualHook: Show a data-leakage path from test results back into selection.
